text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Skopje press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- Charges filed with the Bitola court on Tuesday against a number of people involved in the TAT savings organisation scandal including bank owner Sonja Nikolovska and Bitola mayor Siljan Micevski.
- Unknown persons removed the Macedonian, Albanian and Turkish flags in front of the Debar and Vrutok municipalities Tuesday night, and burned them in Vrutok. The situation in the area is calm.

- Government spokesman Zoran Ivanov said retail outlets of the Skopje oil refinery were demanding an increase of oil derivatives prices. He said the government was making efforts not to raise prices by using internal state resources.
- Macedonia will continue its strategy to join NATO, said Macedonian Foreign Minister Blagoj Handziski.

- The International Finance Corporation (IFC) approved its first loan to Macedonia to the value of $11 million. Out of this amount $5 million will be used for the modernisation of the Grand Hotel in Skopje which will be carried out through a franchise agreement with the U.S. Holiday Inn, $1 million for the Tetex textile industry.

- President of the Democratic Party of Macedonia Tomislav Stojanovski claims arms from Albania are entering Macedonia without any control. On the black markets of Tetovo, Gostivar and the nearby villages, rifles and various military ordnance are being sold at a price from 100 to 300 German marks. -- Mircela Casule, Skopje newsroom +389 91 201 196
